_note: Contract regex-limit v1 (camada-all-2pap): bounded cost of customer `matches` regexes at match time, and the save-time refusal of patterns re2js cannot compile. Byte-identical copies, change all of them together and update the sha256 every suite pins: camada/edge-analyst/test/regex-limit-vectors.json, camada-backend/test/regex-limit-vectors.json, camada-web/src/lib/regex-limit-vectors.json, camada-core/test/fixtures/regex-limit/regex-limit-vectors.json (the server SDKs read this one from the camada-core sibling checkout, like blk5; CAMADA_FIXTURES_DIR overrides). An input value is a string, or {prefix?, repeat, times, suffix?} meaning prefix + repeat x times + suffix. Each row is one rule in snapshot meta form; parse it into a v5 snapshot (camada-core blk5/v5-empty.bin with meta.rules = [rule]) and match the input: hit = the result names the rule. Engine classes: linear = re2js (edge-analyst, camada-core and the JS adapters through it) and Go regexp, which give the true answer; budget = Python regex timeout, Ruby Regexp timeout (3.2+), PHP PCRE match limit, Java deadline CharSequence, .NET matchTimeout, where an over-limit run answers like an over-cap value: hit for block/challenge/warn, miss for skip. over_limit: every engine runs every row and asserts hit[class]. linear_time: linear engines only; hit as given, and a fresh compile plus the first match takes under max_ms (best of 3). refused: patterns re2js refuses (the regex-guard screen accepts most of them; v1.4 below covers the ones it refuses first); edge-analyst validateCond, camada-backend regexError and camada-web regexProblem refuse each with the re2 kind (or the guard text, per v1.4), and, for refused_rule with the pattern as its one condition, every matcher answers cases[].hit[go] in camada-go, edge-analyst and camada-core (and the JS adapters through it), where a pattern Go or re2js refuses never matches (edge-analyst and camada-core since camada-all-rfyr), and hit[native] in the backtracking SDKs, which compile them. accepted: guard- and re2js-accepted patterns no save-time check may refuse. translate: [JS pattern, jsToRe2 output] pairs that the four JS copies (edge-analyst blocklist.js, camada-core path.ts, camada-backend rules-custom.ts, camada-web lib/rules.ts) reproduce exactly with re2js 2.9.0; other languages ignore it. JS without u reads \x not followed by two hex digits as a plain x, and [\b] as a backspace (v1.1, camada-all-2pap review). v1.2: astral surrogate pairs, [\c_]-style class controls, [\B], and - next to a class escape in a class (camada-all-2pap review); rule (d) for that last one was replaced in v1.3 by a refusal (a [\s-z]-style - next to a class escape in a class is refused, never translated). constants: every port asserts its own constant equals the value here. v1.4 (camada-all-mx0h, camada-all-sl00, camada-all-648h): a repeat count written with a leading zero is read as its decimal value, as JS without u reads it. jsToRe2 strips the zeros from each number of an unescaped quantifier brace outside [ ] (a{02} -> a{2}, a{01001} -> a{1001}; [{02}] and \{02} stay as written), and camada-go jsToRE2 reads such a count the same way (pinned for Go by refused RF6 and blk5 LZ1-LZ3, since Go ignores translate). refused also holds patterns the save-time screen refuses before re2js is asked: for such a row (RF5 a{1001} and RF6 a{01001}, both refused first by the camada-all-8r29 repeat-count check) edge-analyst validateCond, camada-backend regexError and camada-web regexProblem answer with the guard's repeat-count text, not the re2 kind, and the row stays in refused because its refused_rule cases pin how a stored pattern saved before that check runs. constants.RE2_DFA_MAX_MEM is the re2js lazy-DFA memory bound per compiled pattern, in bytes (camada-all-sl00); edge-analyst and camada-core assert it and the other ports ignore it, as each port asserts only the constants it has. v1.5 (camada-all-nyy0): accepted drops \u00e9, \Aabc\z and \p{L}: the regex-guard refuses every \u, \A, \z, \p and \P (kind escape), since PHP cannot compile \u and Python cannot compile \z or \p. Their translate rows stay, because stored rules and CVE feed patterns still go through jsToRe2. v1.6 (camada-all-skld): over_limit OL6-OL11 are shapes the regex-guard static screen accepts (its known residuals and its V8 calibration, contracts.md A4): residual A, the 8-level residual B and [0-9]?x12 then (?:a{5}|a{6}|a{7}|a{8}), each as a block row whose input matches and a skip row whose input does not, so every engine class gets the same answer whether or not a budget engine runs out of time (deny hit, skip miss when over); the three patterns are also in accepted. v1.7 (camada-all-4s9z): translate gains x[[:alpha:]]y -> x[\[:alpha:]]y and x[^[:a:]]y -> x[^\[:a:]]y: JS reads a [ inside a class as text, so jsToRe2 writes it as \[ and RE2 never reads [:alpha:] as a POSIX class (camada-all-07c7, camada-all-kdq0); the regex-guard refuses both at save (kind posix), so they are not in accepted. accepted gains x[a-b-\d]y, x[a-z-\w]y and x[\x41-\x5a-\w]y: a - right after a finished class range is a literal, as V8 and RE2 read it (camada-all-uged). v1.8 (camada-all-04la): translate gains x[\S]y -> the JS non-whitespace ranges written out: jsToRe2 expands \S inside [ ] to the code points JS \S matches, since RE2 \S is ASCII-only (camada-all-ao29). translate_refused: JS patterns every jsToRe2 copy refuses with a SyntaxError, never translates (a - next to \s, \d or \w inside [ ], per v1.3; a raw [ inside a class is an atom there, so x[[-\d]y is refused); the four JS suites assert it and other languages ignore it. v1.9 (camada-all-ax9h): accepted_match: x[a-b-\d]y, x[a-z-\w]y and x[\x41-\x5a-\w]y from accepted, run like refused rows (refused_rule with the pattern as its one condition, matched against each case's ua) by every matcher: hit[go] in camada-go, edge-analyst and camada-core (and the JS adapters through it), hit[native] in the backtracking SDKs, each through its own JS translation and engine; the two classes agree on every case. x-y hits because a - right after a finished class range is a literal; the miss rules out a range read through it (xcy for b-d with \d read as d, x^y for \x5a-w), and x.y a class that takes anything. A pattern an engine cannot compile never matches there, so its hit cases fail. camada-backend and camada-web only pin the sha. v1.10 (camada-all-kxym): accepted_match AM1 gains xay and xby, which hit only through the range a-b, so a translation that drops or mangles it (x[a-b-\d]y read as x[-\d]y) fails them; AM2 and AM3 gain no such case, because their ranges a-z and \x41-\x5a (A-Z) lie inside \w in every engine, so no input hits only through the range: AM1 carries the range check. v1.11 (camada-all-k938): refused gains RF7 x😀?y, an astral character written raw then ?: JS without u reads it as two code units and the ? repeats only the low one, RE2 reads one code point and repeats the whole character, so every jsToRe2 copy and camada-go jsToRE2 refuse a written surrogate pair (raw, or escaped as \uD83D\uDE00) right before ? * + or a {n} {n,} {n,m} brace, and the save refuses it with a text that says to put the character in a group (camada-web kind astral); RF7 has no xy case, because the native SDKs split there (Python and Ruby read code points and hit, the others miss as V8 does). v1.11 also (camada-all-cfx4): refused gains RF8 x[😀]?y, an astral character written raw inside [ ]: JS without u reads the class as the two code units of the character, so the pattern hits xy but not x😀y, while RE2 reads one code point and hits both, so every jsToRe2 copy and camada-go jsToRE2 refuse a raw surrogate pair inside [ ] (a range end and a negated class too, ci or not; an escaped \uD83D\uDE00 there stays, as every engine already reads it as two separate halves), and the save refuses it with a text that says to write the character outside the brackets in a group, like x(?:😀|a)y for x[😀a]y (camada-web kind astralClass); RF8 has no x😀y case, because the native SDKs split there (Python and Ruby read code points and hit, the others miss as V8 does). v1.12 (camada-all-k2b3, camada-all-5fxz, camada-all-5lra, camada-all-sy8y): new key astral_split: each row runs like a refused row (refused_rule with the pattern as its one condition, matched against each case's ua) through each engine's own JS translation and engine, and each engine asserts its own key of cases[].hit: go in camada-go, edge-analyst and camada-core (and the JS adapters through it), python, ruby, java, dotnet and php in those SDKs; edge-analyst and camada-core also assert v8, new RegExp(pattern) without u, the reference; camada-backend and camada-web only pin the sha. AS1-AS4 (x.y, x[^a]y, x\Sy, x\Wy on x😀y): an astral character in the input is two code units to JS without u and one code point to re2js, Go, Python and Ruby, so those take it whole and hit where V8, Java (it matches code units, Parser.unitView), .NET (UTF-16) and PHP (PCRE byte mode) miss; accepted, not emulated (camada-all-k2b3; camada-all-vuvo accepted the same for Python and Ruby), because making . or a negated class refuse an astral character would only move the split to AS5 x..y, which V8, Java and .NET hit and the others miss (PHP needs four . for the four bytes). Each AS1-AS5 row also has a case every engine hits, so a miss cannot come from a pattern an engine failed to compile. AS6 x\uD83D and AS7 \uDE00y (camada-all-5fxz): a surrogate half outside a written pair, which V8, Java and .NET match against half of a real character, is a code point no input holds in re2js and Go, so it never matches there (Python and Ruby miss too, PHP cannot compile \u); the save refuses it, every \u spelling as escape (v1.5) and a raw unpaired half with its own text (camada-web kind loneSurrogate), so these rows pin how a stored one reads. A raw unpaired half (or a pair spelled half raw, half escaped) cannot sit in this file: as a JSON escape it is an error to PHP json_decode, Ruby JSON.parse and .NET GetString, and U+FFFD to Go, so the JS repos pin it in their own tests. refused RF7 now has its xy case (go and native false): camada-python and camada-ruby read a quantifier right after a raw astral character as V8 does on well-formed text, the character once when the count allows 1 (? * + {0,1} {1,} and their lazy forms) and never when it does not ({0}, {2}, {2,}) (camada-all-5lra). camada-go jsToRE2 writes an unquantified escaped pair outside [ ] as its code point, as the translate row \uD83D\uDE00 -> \x{1f600} already pins for the JS copies (camada-all-sy8y); Go ignores translate, so camada-go parse_test pins it. v1.13 (camada-all-e20y): new key test_rewrite, [JS pattern, RE2 source] pairs. edge-analyst and camada-core compile a matches pattern from jsToRe2's output with its top-level leading and trailing repeats trimmed (a repeat with min 0 is dropped, {m,n}, {m,} and + become {m}), which is exact for a test anywhere in the value and spares the regex budget a wide no-literal pattern like [^ ]{0,500}[#%] (it compiles as [#%]); a top-level |, a (?flags) setter, \Q or an unknown escape leaves the source unchanged, and a pattern re2js refuses stays refused. The pairs pin that source (re2js 2.9.0) in those two; every other port ignores the key.

over_limit.why: over the limit a deny rule hits although the regex would miss
over the limit a skip rule misses
a skip whose regex truly matches still misses when the limit runs out first
a deny rule hits either way
path regexes run case-insensitively over three path forms; the limit holds there too
regex-guard residual A (camada-all-skld), accepted at save, 272 ms in V8 unbounded: the input matches, so a deny rule hits whether the run finishes or runs out of budget
residual A: the input does not match, so a skip rule misses whether the run finishes or runs out of budget
regex-guard residual B, 8 levels (153 ms V8, 372 ms Python re, unbounded): the input matches, a deny rule hits either way
residual B: the input does not match, a skip rule misses either way (Python regex runs past the 50 ms budget here)
V8-calibrated bar (1.9 ms V8, 330 ms Python re): the input matches, a deny rule hits either way
V8-calibrated bar: the input does not match, a skip rule misses either way

refused.kind: repeat count written with a leading zero
quantifier right after a surrogate pair

accepted_match.kind: literal - between the range a-b and \d
literal - between the range a-z and \w

astral_split.kind: an astral character in the input, read by .
an astral character in the input, read by a negated class
an astral character in the input, read by \S
an astral character in the input, read by \W
an astral character in the input, read by two .
